title: Console roadmap: scope-stripping for alpha operational mode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need to reduce the initial alpha surface for Redwood Console observability so we can ship a defensible operational mode that provides high-value signals (latency, errors, cost rollups) while keeping implementation effort bounded. This ticket documents the scope-stripping plan, acceptance criteria for the alpha, trade-offs, and rollout plan.
background: Original PRD requested broad coverage: per-route token cost, full-span flamegraphs, and long-retention traces. Engineering constraints (kernel scheduling work, telemetry sampling infra) make that unsafe for alpha.

Goal: deliver a small, reliable set of cards and tracing fallback behaviors that let platform and product teams monitor regressions and cost spikes in production without requiring new infra commitments.
This is a product-driven MVP cut to accelerate an alpha release and enable rapid iteration based on real usage signals.
scope_included: Per-route summary cards: request rate (rps), median latency (p50), tail latency (p95), error rate (5xx%).
Aggregate cost rollup per route (daily/7d) using billing tags and existing sampling; no per-token breakdown in alpha.
Trace sampling: head-based sampling for top 10 routes with sampled span timelines and a lightweight waterfall view (no full flamegraph rendering).
Route-level health timeline (30d) with simple anomaly highlight when error rate or latency spikes >2x baseline.
Rollout controls: UI flag to opt into alpha telemetry and a canary exposure flow (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
Telemetry fallbacks: when detailed telemetry not available, show degraded card with explainer and link to diagnostics guide.
scope_cut: Remove per-token cost breakdown and token-level cost attribution in alpha (too high instrumentation cost).
Defer full flamegraph visualizations and heavy trace aggregation to post-alpha (requires backend summary indices).
No long-tail retention (>30d) or advanced trace search in alpha; keep retention to 7-30d depending on data tiering decisions.
Delay per-user or per-subteam cost allocation features to a later engineering sprint.
Exclude automatic root-cause suggestions and AI-based anomaly explanations for alpha release.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: For any route in the alpha cohort, the console shows request rate, p50, p95, and error rate in the route header within 2s of navigation for sampled data.

Cost: The console displays an aggregate daily and 7-day cost estimate for each alpha route, derived from sampled telemetry and billing tags; estimate accuracy within ±25% using sampling reconciliation tests.
Tracing: Top-10 routes by traffic must have sampled traces visible via the lightweight waterfall view; opening a trace should render in <1.5s for typical sampled traces.
Degraded UX: If detailed telemetry is missing for a route, the UI shows a clear degraded state with a one-click link to diagnostics and a message explaining why data is missing.
Rollout: Feature flagging supports staged rollouts and the canary sweep (10% -> 50% -> 100%) can be executed by platform ops without code deploys.
Reliability: Enabling alpha telemetry for up to 20% of traffic across prod clusters must not increase p95 latency for serving requests by more than 3% (monitor via canary test).

Monitoring: Three operational alerts exist for alpha telemetry: telemetry ingestion lag (>2m), sampling-rate regression (>30% deviation), and backend errors (>0.5% error rate) with on-call runbook links.
tradeoffs_and_rationale: Cutting per-token cost attribution reduces immediate product fidelity but avoids high instrumentation and storage costs pre-alpha.
Lightweight waterfall traces provide enough diagnostic context for initial debugging while deferring heavy aggregation work.
Staged rollout and visible degraded UX will help manage support load and set expectations for early adopters.
We accept relaxed cost-estimate accuracy for alpha in exchange for faster time-to-market and lower SRE overhead.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge alpha branch behind feature flag, run internal smoke with dev clusters.
Week 1: Internal pilot (team: Platform + 2 product squads) enablement and fixes.
Week 2: Canary 10% traffic for selected customers, monitor ingestion/latency alerts for 72h.
Week 3: Expand to 50% if canary stable; otherwise rollback and triage in hotfix cycle.
Week 4: General availability for alpha cohort and begin collecting usage signals for post-alpha prioritization.
review_feedback: Engineering: requested to remove per-token billing to avoid cross-team infra changes (noted in ENG-21300).
Design: recommends a placeholder card pattern for degraded telemetry states to reduce cognitive load for early users.
Security: confirmed no new PII is required; standard telemetry GDPR controls apply.
notes: PM will host a scope review sync on 2025-03-14 with Eng and Design to lock acceptance criteria.
Plan to collect qualitative feedback from alpha customers via short follow-up interviews and a 5-question survey.
Post-alpha: re-evaluate per-token cost feature if sampling infra and summary indices land in ENG-21987.
